amendments.normalized_body: The `debug_assert` at nitrogen_cycle.rs:352-355 is vacuous: it checks `alk_budget <= state.water.alkalinity_meq_total + EPSILON`, but at that point `alk_budget` has been decremented (and clamped to ≥0) while `state.water.alkalinity_meq_total` has NOT yet been mutated (the actual pool deduction happens later at line 433-435). The condition `max(initial - costs, 0) <= initial + epsilon` is trivially true for any non-negative costs. Either replace with a meaningful check (e.g., assert that `aob_alk_cost + comammox_alk_cost <= state.water.alkalinity_meq_total + EPSILON` before the `.max(0.0)` clamp, which would catch an over-deduction) or remove it.

In the `closed_system_alkalinity_mass_balance` test (nitrification_alkalinity.rs:156-165), the lower bound on `observed_ratio` is `NITRIFICATION_ALK_MEQ_PER_MG_N * 0.80` (80% of stoichiometric constant). The comment explains biomass growth diverts ~5% of TAN away from oxidation, so the ratio should be ~95% of the constant. An 80% lower bound is a 20% tolerance that would pass even if nearly a quarter of the alkalinity accounting were lost. Consider tightening to 0.90 (or even 0.92) to make this regression test more sensitive to real accounting errors while still accommodating the growth-yield pathway.

Include `crates/tank_core/tests/nitrification_alkalinity.rs:1-336` in version control. It is currently untracked (`git status` shows `??`), so the actual patch produced by `git diff` does not contain any of the new acceptance-criteria coverage for nitrification-driven alkalinity depletion, pH decline, or the soft-vs-hard buffering contrast.

Fix the new tracing metric exposed from `crates/tank_core/src/systems/nitrogen_cycle.rs:13-23,343-346` and logged in `crates/tank_core/src/engine.rs:229-239`. `total_mg_n_nitrified` is reported as `nob_step + comammox_step` (nitrate produced), while alkalinity consumption is computed from `aob_step + comammox_step` (TAN oxidation). In ticks where AOB outruns NOB and nitrite accumulates, the trace will report little or zero `nitrogen_cycle.total_n_nitrified_mg` alongside a non-zero `nitrogen_cycle.alk_consumed_meq`. Either rename the metric to nitrate production or change it to total TAN oxidation so the diagnostics stay internally consistent.

Add a reusable alkalinity-return accounting surface instead of only a constant. `crates/tank_core/src/types/process.rs:19-27` defines `DENITRIFICATION_ALK_MEQ_PER_MG_N`, but the public/runtime interface is still nitrification-only (`NitrogenCycleOutput::alkalinity_consumed_meq` in `crates/tank_core/src/systems/nitrogen_cycle.rs:15-23` and the hard-coded `nitrogen_cycle.alk_consumed_meq` note in `crates/tank_core/src/engine.rs:236-238`). E4b will still need another API/trace-schema change to represent alkalinity return, so the promised denitrification return path is not actually prepared yet.
